en: Homage to the Omniscient One.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of monks.
Together with twelve hundred and fifty monks— renowned elders and great disciples, all of whom were arhats—
such as the elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, and Mahākāśyapa.
And with Mahākapphiṇa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Śuddhipanthaka, Nanda, Ananda, Rāhula, Gavāmpati, Bharadvāja, Kālodayin, Vakkula, and Aniruddha.
And with these and many other great śrāvakas, and with many bodhisattvas mahāsattvas,
such as Mañjuśrī the Youthful and Ajita.
And by the bodhisattva Gandhahastin, the bodhisattva Nityodyukta,
and the bodhisattva Anikṣiptadhura.
Together with these and many other bodhisattva mahāsattvas,
as well as Śakra, the lord of the gods, and Brahmā, the sovereign of the Sahā world.
Together with these and many other hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sons of gods. //1//
Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Śāriputra:
"Śāriputra, in the western direction, beyond a hundred thousand million buddha-fields from this buddha-field, there is a world-system named Sukhāvatī."

There, a Tathāgata named Amitāyus, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, currently resides, remains, and maintains himself, and he teaches the Dharma. What do you think, Śāriputra, for what reason is that world-system [called Sukhāvatī]?
It is called "Sukhāvatī.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that world-system Sukhāvatī, there is no physical suffering for sentient beings, nor any mental suffering; there are only immeasurable causes of happiness.
For that reason, that world-system is called Sukhāvatī. //2//

Furthermore, Śāriputra, the world-system Sukhāvatī is adorned all around and encircled by seven railings, seven rows of palm trees, and networks of tinkling bells made of the four precious substances; it is variegated and beautiful to behold.
That is to say, Śāriputra, with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal.
That buddha-field is beautifully adorned. //3//
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the world-system Sukhāvatī there are lotus ponds made of the seven precious substances,
namely: gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, red pearl, emerald, and musāragalva as the seventh precious substance.
They are filled with water endowed with the eight qualities, with level banks that can be drunk from by crows,
and strewn with golden sands.
And in those lotus ponds, on all four sides, there were four staircases, variegated and beautiful, made of the four precious substances,
namely: gold, silver, beryl, and crystal.
It is made of crystal;
and all around those lotus ponds, beautiful and wonderful jewel-trees made of the seven precious substances have grown.
Namely, of gold, silver, beryl,
crystal, red pearl, emerald, and musāragalva as the seventh jewel. And in those lotus ponds, blue lotuses have grown.
Blue, blue-colored, blue-appearing, and blue-shining; yellow, yellow-colored, yellow-appearing, and yellow-shining; red, red-colored, red-appearing, and red-shining; white...
They were white in color, white in luster, and white in appearance; they were variegated, of variegated color,
variegated in luster, and variegated in appearance, with a circumference equal to that of a chariot wheel.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field. //4//
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field divine musical instruments resound perpetually, and the great earth is golden-colored and delightful;
and in that buddha-field...
Three times during the night and three times during the day, a rain of divine *māndārava* flowers falls;
and those beings who have been reborn there [are satisfied] by a single morning meal.
Having gone to other world-systems, they pay homage to hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas;
and having showered each Tathāgata with hundreds of thousands of millions of flower rains, they return once more to that very same world-system for their midday rest.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field. //5//
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field there are swans, cranes, and peacocks;
three times during the night and three times during the day they gather together and perform musical concerts, uttering their respective cries.
As they speak,
the sound of the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment issues forth;
there, among those humans, that sound—

Upon hearing this, attention directed toward the Buddha arises, attention directed toward the Dharma arises, and attention directed toward the Saṅgha arises. What do you think, Śāriputra? Are those beings truly born into the animal realm? You should not view it in that way.
For what reason?
Śāriputra, even the name of hells, of animal births, or of the world of Yama does not exist there in that buddha-field.
There are none. Furthermore, those flocks of birds were emanated by that Tathāgata Amitāyus to emit the sound of the Dharma.
Śāriputra, it is with such arrays of qualities of the Buddha-field as these [that he is adorned].
That buddha-field is beautifully adorned. //6//
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field, when those rows of palm trees and those networks of tinkling bells are stirred by the wind, a beautiful and pleasing sound issues forth.
Śāriputra, it is just like, for example, the sound of a divine musical instrument consisting of hundreds of thousands of millions of parts.
Just as a beautiful and charming sound issues forth when played by masters, even so,
Śāriputra, from those rows of palm trees and those networks of small bells, a beautiful and charming sound issues forth when stirred by the wind.

There, when those humans hear that sound, mindfulness of the Buddha becomes established in their bodies, mindfulness of the Dharma becomes established in their bodies, and mindfulness of the Saṅgha becomes established in their bodies.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field. //7//
What do you think, Śāriputra? For what reason is that Tathāgata called Amitāyus?
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the measure of the lifespan of that Tathāgata and of those humans is indeed immeasurable.
For that reason, that Tathāgata is called Amitāyus.
And, Śāriputra, ten kalpas have passed since that Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. //8//
What do you think, Śāriputra? For what reason is that Tathāgata called Amitābha? Indeed, Śāriputra, the light of that Tathāgata is unimpeded throughout all Buddha-fields.
For that reason, that Tathāgata is called Amitābha.
And, Śāriputra, that Tathāgata’s assembly of disciples is immeasurable— those pure Arhats whose number is not easily able to be stated.
It is with such [disciples], Śāriputra, [that he is endowed].
That buddha-field is beautifully adorned with the arrays of qualities of a buddha-field. //9//
Furthermore, Śāriputra, as for those beings who have been born in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitāyus— pure bodhisattvas who are irreversible and bound to only one more birth—
it is not easy, Śāriputra, to state the measure of those bodhisattvas.
Elsewhere, they are reckoned as being immeasurable and incalculable.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, beings in that buddha-field must make a vow.
Why is that?
For when one comes into association with such noble persons as these,
it is not by mere inferiority alone.
Śāriputra, by virtue of their roots of merit, beings are reborn in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Śāriputra, if any son of good family or daughter of good family hears the name of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, and having heard it, brings it to mind;

Whether for one night, two nights, three nights, four nights, five nights, six nights, or seven nights, that son of good family or daughter of good family will attend to it with an undistracted mind; when that son of good family or daughter of good family passes away, at the time of his passing—
As he practices, that Tathāgata Amitāyus, surrounded by the community of śrāvakas and preceded by the host of bodhisattvas,
will stand before him; with an undistorted mind,
he will pass away, and having passed away, he will be reborn in the buddha-field of that very Tathāgata Amitāyus, in Sukhāvatī.
One will be reborn in that world-system.
Therefore, Śāriputra, seeing this purpose, I say: a son of good family or a daughter of good family should, with reverence, [direct their thoughts] toward that buddha-field.
One should make a mental aspiration. //10//
Just as I now proclaim them here, Śāriputra, even so in the eastern direction there are Tathāgatas named Akṣobhya, Merudhvaja, Mahāmeru, and Meruprabhāsa.

Śāriputra, with the Tathāgata named Mañjudhvaja as their leader, Buddhas and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the eastern direction cover their respective Buddha-fields with their tongue-organs and perform this proclamation.
You should all believe in this Dharma discourse called "The Acceptance by All Buddhas," which proclaims inconceivable qualities. //11//
In this way, Śāriputra, in the southern direction there are Tathāgatas such as the one named Candrasūryapradīpa, the one named Yaśaḥprabha, the one named Mahārciskandha, the one named Merupradīpa,
and the one named Anantavīrya; these and others are the foremost Tathāgatas in the south.
In every direction, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, covering their respective Buddha-fields with their tongue-faculties, are making this declaration:
"Have faith!"
You [should uphold] this Dharma discourse named "The Praise of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas. //12//
Likewise, in the western direction, there are the Tathāgata named Amitāyus, the Tathāgata named Amitaskandha, the Tathāgata named Amitadhvaja, the Tathāgata named Mahāprabha,
the Tathāgata named Mahāratnaketu, the Tathāgata named Śuddharaśmiprabha, and others headed by these.

Śāriputra, in the western direction, Buddhas, Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongue-faculties, are making this declaration.
You should all take up this Dharma discourse named "The Acceptance by All Buddhas," which proclaims inconceivable qualities. //13//
Likewise, in the northern direction, there is the Tathāgata named Mahārciskaṃdha, the Tathāgata named Vaiśvānaranirghoṣa, the Tathāgata named Dundubhisvaranirghoṣa,
the Tathāgata named Duṣpradharṣa, the Tathāgata named Ādityasaṃbhava, and the Tathāgata named Jaleniprabha.

Śāriputra, there are Buddhas, Blessed Ones, in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, headed by the Tathāgata named Prabhākara; each of these [Buddhas]— their own respective...
Covering the Buddha-fields with their tongue-faculties, they perform this proclamation:
"Believe this Dharma discourse named 'The Praise of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas. //14//

In this way, Śāriputra, in the direction below, there are the Tathāgata named Siṃha, the Tathāgata named Yaśas, the Tathāgata named Yaśaḥprabhāsa, the Tathāgata named Dharma, the Tathāgata named Dharmadhara, the Tathāgata named Dharmadhvaja, and others headed by these.
In every direction, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongue-faculties, perform this declaration:
"Believe this discourse on the proclamation of inconceivable qualities, called 'The Acceptance by All Buddhas'."
the discourse on the Dharma. //15//
Likewise, in the direction above, there is the Tathāgata named Brahmaghoṣa,
the Tathāgata named Nakṣatrarāja, the Tathāgata named Indraketudhvajarāja, the Tathāgata named Gandhottama, the Tathāgata named Gandhaprabhāsa, and the Tathāgata named Mahārciskandha.
The Tathāgata named Ratnakusumasaṃpuṣpitagātra, the Tathāgata named Sālendrarāja, the Tathāgata named Ratnotpalaśrī, the Tathāgata named Sarvārthadarśa,
and the Tathāgata named Sumerukalpa— Śāriputra, these and others such as these are in the direction above.
Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongue-faculties, make this declaration:
"Believe this!"
The Dharma discourse named "The Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas. //16//
What do you think, Śāriputra? For what reason is this Dharma-discourse called "The Acceptance by All Buddhas"?
Śāriputra, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family shall hear the name of this Dharma-discourse, [they shall be sustained] by those Blessed Buddhas.
All those who shall uphold this name will be sustained by the Buddhas and shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Therefore, Śāriputra, [you should do so].
Have faith, believe, and do not doubt me and those Blessed Buddhas.
Śāriputra, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family shall make a mental vow for that Buddha-field of the Blessed Tathāgata Amitāyus, [they shall all be born there].
Whether they have already done so, are doing so, or will do so, all of them will become irreversible from unexcelled [enlightenment];
they will be born, have been born, or are being born in that buddha-field.
Therefore, Śāriputra, faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family [should aspire] to that buddha-field.
One should generate the mental aspiration. //17//
Just as, Śāriputra, I now proclaim the inconceivable qualities of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
even so, Śāriputra, do those Buddhas [proclaim] mine.
The Blessed Ones thus proclaim such inconceivable qualities:
"A most difficult task has been performed by the Blessed Śākyamuni, the sovereign king of the Śākyas."

Having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this Sahā world-system, he taught a Dharma that is contrary to the expectations of the entire world, amidst the degeneration of the eon, the degeneration of sentient beings, the degeneration of views, the degeneration of lifespan, and the degeneration of afflictions. //18//

Therefore, Śāriputra, it is also extremely difficult for me that, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in the Sahā world-system, I have taught a Dharma that is contrary to the expectations of the entire world— amidst the corruption of sentient beings, the corruption of views, the corruption of afflictions, the corruption of lifespan, and the corruption of the eon. //19//
The Blessed One spoke thus, and the Venerable Śāriputra,
those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas were uplifted in mind by the Blessed One.
They rejoiced in what was spoken. //20//
The Mahāyāna Sūtra titled *Sukhāvatīvyūha* (The Array of Sukhāvatī).
